today.h: Software Broke First: Dow -1.64%, S&P Lowest Since Late July
today.d: Salesforce fell 9.45% after Business Insider reported it is capping employee AI spending, and the software complex took the S&P 76.06 points lower to 7,340.53, its lowest close since late July. The Dow lost 848.75 points with 25 of its 30 members down, the VIX rose 11.13% to 25.46, and chips went the other way: the SOX added 0.34% and Nvidia guided fourth-quarter revenue to $130.0 billion after the bell.
today.c1:
The fourth straight loss was a software loss. Salesforce fell 9.45% to $194.52 after Business Insider reported the company is setting monthly AI token budgets - $1,000 for technical roles and $100 for others - following a quarter in which some employees spent thousands of dollars a month on tokens. Intuit fell 7.17%, ServiceNow 6.51%, Workday 5.80%, Adobe 4.25% and Oracle 3.43%, and the selling spread through the tape one day before Anthropic is expected to price its IPO above the $70-$78 range.

The Dow lost 848.75 points, or 1.64%, to 50,759.42, with 25 of its 30 components lower; the S&P 500 fell 76.06 points, or 1.03%, to 7,340.53, its lowest close since late July, and the Nasdaq 181.37 points, or 0.74%, to 24,328.38. Breadth was worse than the indexes: 17 of every 20 S&P 500 stocks fell, the equal-weight RSP lost 1.45% against the SPY's 1.01%, and the two sectors that were green on 11/16 - utilities and staples - fell 1.59% and 1.23%. The VIX rose 11.13% to 25.46 after touching 27.73, a fourth straight gain.

The split was in chips. The SOX rose 0.34%, Broadcom added 2.46% and Arm 4.76%, and after the close Nvidia reported $115.8 billion of revenue against a $109.1 billion consensus and guided the fourth quarter to $130.0 billion, sending the shares more than 2% higher in after-hours trading.
today.c4:
• The break: Salesforce -9.45% on AI-token budgets and 25 of 30 Dow names lower explain the 1.64% Dow drop.
  • The tell: 17 of 20 S&P stocks fell and RSP -1.45% was worse than SPY's -1.01%, so this was not a megacap story.
  • The split: the SOX +0.34% and Nvidia's $130.0 billion guide, more than 2% higher after hours.
  • The calendar: Anthropic prices 11/18 and trades 11/19 as ANT; FOMC 12/8-9.

Energy leads at +41.71%, health is second at +19.66%, staples third at +17.74%, technology fourth at +13.40% and materials fifth at +12.11%; real estate (+8.03%) is the only other sector ahead of the index. Communications -10.58% and consumer discretionary -1.93% are the only sectors down. The referee is the 10Y at 5.10%, 92bp above where 2025 ended, with the front end up 133bp and 2s10s 41bp flatter. The average stock is 5.22 points ahead of the index, and the two assets bought as hedges, gold and bitcoin, are both lower.
ytd.c4:
• The engine: energy +41.71% and health +19.66%, with staples +17.74% third and technology +13.40% fourth.
  • The referee: a 92bp 10Y and a 133bp 2Y, with 2s10s 41bp flatter.
  • The breadth: the average stock is 5.22 points ahead, and two sectors are down.
  • The failed hedges: gold -10.99% and bitcoin -26.85% in a year when CPI ran hot.

chains.t: ① Energy and Health Lead, Tech Falls to Fourth
steps: The S&P is +7.23% at 7,340.53, the Nasdaq +4.67% at 24,328.38 and the Dow +5.61% at 50,759.42
Energy +41.71% is the biggest sector gain; health +19.66%, staples +17.74%, technology +13.40%, materials +12.11% and real estate +8.03% are the only other sectors ahead of the index
The referee is the 10Y, 92bp above the 12/31/2025 4.18%
The average stock is ahead: RSP +12.63% against SPY's +7.41%, 5.22 points
Communications -10.58% and consumer discretionary -1.93% are the only sectors down
chains.d: The year still has an engine and a referee: energy, health and staples ahead of technology, against a 10Y 92bp higher, which leaves the S&P at +7.23% instead of more.

news.fact: The S&P 500 closed 2025 at 6,845.50; it closed at 7,340.53 on 11/17, a gain of 7.23%.
The Dow closed at 50,759.42 versus 48,063.29 at the end of 2025, a gain of 5.61%.
The Nasdaq Composite closed at 24,328.38 versus 23,241.99 at the end of 2025, a gain of 4.67%.

chains.t: ② The Year's Rate Bill: 92bp, and 133bp at the Front End
steps: The 10Y is 92bp higher at 5.10% and the 30Y 62bp higher at 5.46%
The 2Y is 133bp higher at 4.80%, so 2s10s has flattened 41bp over the year to 30bp
December is fully priced for a hike, which is why the front end carries the year
chains.d: The year's rate bill is 92bp at the 10Y and 133bp at the 2Y: the front end did the work, the curve flattened 41bp, and December is fully priced.

news.fact: The 10-year Treasury yield was 5.10% versus 4.18% on 12/31/2025, the 30-year 5.46% versus 4.84% and the 2-year 4.80% versus 3.47%.
January Brent settled at $93.14 versus $60.85 at the end of 2025, and December WTI at $86.01 versus $57.42.

chains.t: ③ Nine Sectors Up, and Two Hedges That Failed
steps: Nine of 11 sectors are higher and the median sector (+8.03%) beat the index's +7.23%
Gold is -10.99% at $3,864.20 and bitcoin -26.85% at $64,008 - the two hedges that did not pay
The dollar is +5.36% on the DXY at 103.55
The Russell 2000 is +8.86% and the VIX is 70.30% higher at 25.46
chains.d: Breadth is the year's surprise: the median sector beat the index, and the two assets bought as insurance, gold and bitcoin, are both lower.

news.fact: Gold futures settled at $3,864.20, down 10.99% from 12/31/2025's $4,341.10.
The dollar index closed at 103.55, up 5.36% from 12/31/2025's 98.28.
The VIX closed at 25.46, up 70.30% from 12/31/2025's 14.95.

chains.t: ④ Nvidia Is the Year's Broken Leader
steps: Nvidia is -16.64% at $155.46 from 12/31/2025's $186.50, after trading at a record $239.24 on 10/6
The rest of the complex is still up: AMD +135.06% and Micron +149.61%
The SOXX is +40.92% for the year, so the ETF is positive while the name that built the trade is not
Semis peaked on 6/22 and the SOXX is 35.2% below that close of $218.34
chains.d: The AI trade split in two: memory and AMD are up 135% to 150% while Nvidia, the index it built, is 16.64% lower for the year.

news.fact: Nvidia closed at $155.46, down 16.64% from 12/31/2025's $186.50.
SOXX closed at $141.46, up 40.92% from 12/31/2025's $100.38 and 35.2% below its 6/22 record of $218.34.
